vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: intelligent-continuous-re
Version: 4.0.0

The skill bundle contains a comprehensive methodology for AI-augmented requirements engineering (v4). It provides structured instructions (R0-R10) for an agent to assist in project planning, stakeholder analysis, and documentation. No malicious code, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injections were found; the content is purely instructional and aligned with its stated purpose.

llm.summary: This is an instruction-only requirements-engineering skill that describes an AI‑assisted RE process; its instructions, lack of installs, and requested resources are consistent with that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the content of SKILL.md: it documents an AI-augmented continuous requirements engineering workflow. No unexpected binaries, packages, or credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is a prose methodology and templates for running an RE process. It references actions like 'LLM scans historical project data' and 'NLP自动提取用户反馈/日志' which are conceptual; the file does not contain concrete commands, file-system paths, or external endpoints. This is mostly fine, but the phrasing is ambiguous about where historical data comes from and how it will be accessed — a runtime implementation would need explicit limits.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. Nothing will be written to disk by the skill itself during install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables, credentials, or config paths are declared. The skill's claimed capabilities don't demand extra secrets or system access as presented.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent and low-risk because it only provides process guidance (no code, no installs, no secret requests). Before using it, confirm where any 'historical project data' or logs would come from: avoid pointing the agent at sensitive system directories or private credentials. If you turn this into an automated workflow, restrict the data sources the agent can read (project docs, selected repos) and review audit/logging for any data sent to external services. If you need the agent to operate on private data, test in a sandbox and explicitly approve the data sources first.
